chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa said:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mutatayyib wrote to him: 'Afterwards, may Allah the Exalted prolong your life, we inform you, O our Master, that we are in doubt regarding this will which Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Daryab bequeathed. This is because the freedmen and righteous slaves of our Master mentioned that the deceased does not have the right to bequeath more than one-third of his wealth if he has children. Muhammad ibn Yahya had bequeathed more than half of what he left from his estate. If our Master and Lord (may Allah prolong his stay) sees fit to lift this veil of obscurity that we have complained about and clarify this for us, we will act upon it, God willing.' He replied: 'If he bequeathed it before he had children, his bequest is valid, because his child was born after him. And that which confirms what we mentioned is that the bequest is not valid for what exceeds one-third.'
ai.seo_question: Is a will exceeding one-third of the estate valid if the deceased had no children at the time of making it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar resolves a specific juristic dispute regarding the temporal validity of a will exceeding one-third when the deceased has offspring, a key issue in Shia inheritance law. The scholar clarifies that the bequest remains valid if made prior to the birth of children, but the excess over the one-third limit is void if made after their birth, aligning with the principle that the one-third restriction applies to the estate at the time of death. This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on the precise timing of legal acts relative to the existence of heirs.
